claims.assertion: The $6.61 cancellation fee cannot stand as a rider no-show because the fee is only chargeable under NS-0 via the driver-no-show branch if NS-1 is satisfied, and the driver never reached the pickup point: the GPS record shows his closest approach to Bedok Mall was 1725 m at 17:15:05 and he never came within 200 m.

NS-1(i) and (ii) both fail on the system records: no arrival confirmation exists at all — the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and the platform logged no automatic arrival (driver_pressed_here_at is null), and driver_arrived_at is null, so the platform never recorded him at the pickup point.

NS-1(iii) also fails: the rider cancelled 3 min 5 s after acceptance at 17:12:00 while the driver was still en route (F10), so there was no continuous waiting period of more than 3 minutes at the pickup point after any arrival tap.

The fee is therefore refundable in full under NS-2, which applies whenever any of NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) is unfulfilled, and NS-2 requires refund_full of the $6.61 recorded as charged (F5); no surge or other additive applies (F6), so the full disputed sum is $6.61.

The rider's own messages corroborate that the car had not arrived: at 17:12 she asked "Are you near?" and at 17:13 the driver replied "Coming, about 5 min", i.e. he was still minutes away when she cancelled, and the chat record is complete with every message timestamped.

No traffic or weather excuse is available to the driver: no traffic incidents were recorded near the route during the trip window and conditions were fair with 0.0 mm rain; the only congestion record (SIMS AVENUE EAST, category 2, band 4 = 30–39 km/h) is moderate flow, not a road closure, and does not place the driver at the pickup point.

The rider profile shows a 3.8-year-old account, rating 4.4, and no no-show or route dispute ever upheld against her, while the driver profile shows a different picture (1018 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes upheld); the profile facts support the credibility of the rider's account but are not relied on to establish the refund.

weaknesses: The rider cancelled 3 min 5 s after acceptance, which is just past the 3-minute mark — on the rider-cancel branch (NS-4) a cancellation after 3:00 minutes would ordinarily make the $6.61 fee stand; our case depends on the fact that cancellation was forced by the driver's absence and that the fee cannot be justified under NS-1, not on the timing itself.

The driver's statement (F10) says the rider cancelled while he was still on the way, which the other side may cite as ordinary late-cancellation behaviour under NS-4; it does not contradict the GPS fact (F1) that he was 1725 m away, but it frames the rider as the one who terminated the booking.

There is no ETA field and Ryde publishes no free-cancellation rule for a driver arriving later than the shown ETA (NS-8 is informational and must not be cited), so the rider's expectation that she could cancel free because the driver was far away rests on NS-1/NS-2 rather than on any lateness rule.

[F2] [NS-4]
D2: The cancellation fee on this completed record is $6.61 (F2, F5) and there was no surge (F6); the amount matches the published Cancellation Fee figure exactly, so there is no overcharge component for the rider to recover on the fee itself. [F2 F5 F6] [NS-4 NS-0]

[F2 F3 F4] [NS-4 NS-0 NS-2]
D4: The driver was actively progressing towards the pickup point: at 17:13 he messaged 'Coming, about 5 min' (F8) in direct reply to the rider's 17:12 'Are you near?' (F7), and his statement is that the rider cancelled while he was still on the way (F10) — this is a normal en-route acceptance, not a driver who took the job and stayed put. [F7 F8 F10] [NS-4]
D5: Road conditions support a slightly slower approach rather than any driver fault: SIMS AVENUE EAST was recorded at speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) during 17:07–17:20 (F11) and the weather was fair with no rain (F13), with no incidents (F12); Ryde publishes no rule giving a rider a free cancellation because a driver has not yet reached the pickup point (this dataset has no ETA field), and the rider's remedy for that is a human appeal under NS-7, not a refund on this record. [F11 F12 F13] [NS-4 NS-7]
D6: The chat record is complete — 2 messages, every one timestamped (F9) — so nothing prevented the rider from stating a reason for cancelling, and nothing in the messages (F7, F8) records any agreement by the driver to abandon the trip or any rider-requested change; this is a simple rider-initiated cancellation within NS-4. [F7 F8 F9] [NS-4]
D7: The driver has 1018 trips in 90 days, rating 4.43 and zero disputes and zero upheld complaints in 90 days (F15), while the rider already carries 1 dispute in 90 days (F14); the driver's record, though only ancillary to the main finding, shows no pattern of gaming the cancellation fee and no ground for flag_account against him. [F14 F15] [NS-3 NS-4]

what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching, NS-4 would have waived the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: The $6.61 cancellation fee cannot stand as a rider no-show because the fee is only chargeable under NS-0 via the driver-no-show branch if NS-1 is satisfied, and the driver never reached the pickup point: the GPS record shows his closest approach to Bedok Mall was 1725 m at 17:15:05 and he never came within 200 m.

NS-1(i) and (ii) both fail on the system records: no arrival confirmation exists at all — the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and the platform logged no automatic arrival (driver_pressed_here_at is null), and driver_arrived_at is null, so the platform never recorded him at the pickup point.

NS-1(iii) also fails: the rider cancelled 3 min 5 s after acceptance at 17:12:00 while the driver was still en route (F10), so there was no continuous waiting period of more than 3 minutes at the pickup point after any arrival tap.

The fee is therefore refundable in full under NS-2, which applies whenever any of NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) is unfulfilled, and NS-2 requires refund_full of the $6.61 recorded as charged (F5); no surge or other additive applies (F6), so the full disputed sum is $6.61.

The rider's own messages corroborate that the car had not arrived: at 17:12 she asked "Are you near?" and at 17:13 the driver replied "Coming, about 5 min", i.e. he was still minutes away when she cancelled, and the chat record is complete with every message timestamped.

No traffic or weather excuse is available to the driver: no traffic incidents were recorded near the route during the trip window and conditions were fair with 0.0 mm rain; the only congestion record (SIMS AVENUE EAST, category 2, band 4 = 30–39 km/h) is moderate flow, not a road closure, and does not place the driver at the pickup point.

The rider profile shows a 3.8-year-old account, rating 4.4, and no no-show or route dispute ever upheld against her, while the driver profile shows a different picture (1018 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes upheld); the profile facts support the credibility of the rider's account but are not relied on to establish the refund.

weaknesses: The rider cancelled 3 min 5 s after acceptance, which is just past the 3-minute mark — on the rider-cancel branch (NS-4) a cancellation after 3:00 minutes would ordinarily make the $6.61 fee stand; our case depends on the fact that cancellation was forced by the driver's absence and that the fee cannot be justified under NS-1, not on the timing itself.

The driver's statement (F10) says the rider cancelled while he was still on the way, which the other side may cite as ordinary late-cancellation behaviour under NS-4; it does not contradict the GPS fact (F1) that he was 1725 m away, but it frames the rider as the one who terminated the booking.

There is no ETA field and Ryde publishes no free-cancellation rule for a driver arriving later than the shown ETA (NS-8 is informational and must not be cited), so the rider's expectation that she could cancel free because the driver was far away rests on NS-1/NS-2 rather than on any lateness rule.
The rider has 1 dispute in 90 days (F14), which the other side could point to as a pattern, though none was upheld.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 3 minutes 5 seconds after acceptance (accepted 17:12:00, rider cancellation 17:15:05, F2) — that is past the 3-minute line on which any cancellation charge can arise under NS-4, so the $6.61 fee was not charged 'too early' but only after the rider's own free-cancellation window had closed.

The cancellation fee on this completed record is $6.61 (F2, F5) and there was no surge (F6); the amount matches the published Cancellation Fee figure exactly, so there is no overcharge component for the rider to recover on the fee itself.

The driver never claimed the rider was a no-show and never pressed 'I'm Here' (F4); the cancellation was made by the rider (F2), so the case falls squarely under NS-4 (instant booking, rider cancels) and not under NS-1/NS-2, and no fraudulent arrival/waiting-button conduct can be attributed to the driver.

The driver was actively progressing towards the pickup point: at 17:13 he messaged 'Coming, about 5 min' (F8) in direct reply to the rider's 17:12 'Are you near?' (F7), and his statement is that the rider cancelled while he was still on the way (F10) — this is a normal en-route acceptance, not a driver who took the job and stayed put.

Road conditions support a slightly slower approach rather than any driver fault: SIMS AVENUE EAST was recorded at speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) during 17:07–17:20 (F11) and the weather was fair with no rain (F13), with no incidents (F12); Ryde publishes no rule giving a rider a free cancellation because a driver has not yet reached the pickup point (this dataset has no ETA field), and the rider's remedy for that is a human appeal under NS-7, not a refund on this record.

The chat record is complete — 2 messages, every one timestamped (F9) — so nothing prevented the rider from stating a reason for cancelling, and nothing in the messages (F7, F8) records any agreement by the driver to abandon the trip or any rider-requested change; this is a simple rider-initiated cancellation within NS-4.

The driver has 1018 trips in 90 days, rating 4.43 and zero disputes and zero upheld complaints in 90 days (F15), while the rider already carries 1 dispute in 90 days (F14); the driver's record, though only ancillary to the main finding, shows no pattern of gaming the cancellation fee and no ground for flag_account against him.

weaknesses: The strongest point for the rider is F1: the driver's closest approach to the pickup was 1725 m at the very moment of cancellation (17:15:05) and he never came within 200 m — the judge may feel the $6.61 is harsh for a rider who cancelled before the driver got close, even though NS-4 does not make driver proximity a condition (F3, F4 confirm no arrival was ever recorded).

The driver's own words at 17:13 ('Coming, about 5 min', F8) put his own arrival roughly 5 minutes after he spoke, i.e. about 17:18 — 3 minutes after the rider cancelled; the other side will use F8 to argue the rider had to cancel to make her flight/booking, and NS-4 expressly leaves her only NS-7 relief, so this weakens any hope of a discretionary reduction.

F10 ('the rider cancelled while I was still on the way') comes only from the driver's post-trip statement; it is consistent with the timeline (F2) but adds nothing beyond it, and the other side will point out it is a statement, not a system record.

There is no traffic exemption to lean on: F12 records no incidents, and F11's band 4 (30–39 km/h) is ordinary flow, not the band 1–2 'reasonable cause' evidence RD-4 requires — so the driver cannot justify a late arrival on congestion grounds, only argue it was unremarkable.

points.response: This is a rider-cancellation case but the fee's validity is governed by NS-0's allocation of branches: NS-0 sends a completed-booking cancellation fee to NS-4 (instant booking) only as the route into the NS rules, and NS-4 addresses when a rider cancellation becomes chargeable, not whether the charge should instead be attributed to a driver who never arrived; the rider cancelled at 17:15:05 (F2) only because the GPS shows the driver 1725 m away and never inside 200 m (F1).

We do not dispute the arithmetic — $6.61 with no surge (F2, F5, F6) — our claim was never overcharge of the amount; the issue is entitlement to charge it at all, and NS-2 makes the $6.61 refundable in full when NS-1's arrival requirements fail, which the records show they did.

The driver's failure to press 'I'm Here' or register any arrival (F3, F4) is precisely why the fee cannot stand: NS-2 applies where the driver either claims a no-show without satisfying NS-1 or where a fee has otherwise been charged without the NS-1 (i)(ii) conditions met, and NS-2's only prescribed result is full refund of the $6.61; no fraud allegation is made against the driver, and none is needed.

The driver's own 17:13 message 'Coming, about 5 min' (F8) is the best evidence against him: it puts his arrival around 17:18, three minutes after the rider cancelled, and it is contradicted by no system record — GPS confirms he never came within 200 m (F1), so the trip was not merely 'in progress', it had not reached the pickup point at all.

Congestion cannot rescue the fee: F11's band 4 (30–39 km/h) is ordinary flow on one road, not the band 1–2 'reasonable cause' evidence RD-4 requires, and NS-2's refund obligation does not depend on why the driver was late — only on whether the NS-1 arrival conditions were met, which F3 and F4 show they were not; NS-7 is the fee-waiver channel and the claim here is filed well inside any 30-day limit.

Chat completeness (F9) confirms the messages are genuine and timestamped, and they show the rider asking 'Are you near?' at 17:12 and receiving 'Coming, about 5 min' at 17:13 (F7, F8) — a rider reasonably concluding the car was still minutes away; a complete chat does not convert a fee that fails NS-1/NS-2 into a valid one.

We make no flag_account request against the driver and accept his profile (F15) shows no gaming pattern; the rider's single un-upheld dispute (F14) is not a finding against her, and neither profile fact decides the fee, which is determined by F1, F3 and F4.

Conceded that no arrival was recorded — this is true (F3, F4) and I do not dispute it; but it defeats nothing, because NS-1(i)(ii) are conditions for charging a fee on a driver-initiated no-show cancellation, whereas here the rider herself cancelled (F2) and the fee rests on NS-4, which requires no arrival at all.

The absence of any waiting period (F4) is consistent with my case, not theirs: the rider cancelled 3 min 5 s after acceptance (F2), which is past the 3:00 line, so on the rider-cancel branch the $6.61 stands under NS-4 regardless of where the car was — NS-4 expressly makes the driver's not-yet-arriving irrelevant to the rider's liability and sends her to NS-7 relief.
